subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw support gateway-side credential forwarding for this case?
rationale: This decides whether node hosts may acquire and transfer provider OAuth refresh-token material for gateway-owned model runtime, which is both a product UX choice and a credential-boundary decision.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block auth login when node-host config points at a non-loopback gateway and instruct the user to run the command on the gateway host.

options.title: Design gateway credential forwarding
options.body: Add an authenticated gateway-side flow that stores provider credentials only in the gateway auth store without first consuming them into the node-local store.

options.title: Warn but allow local write
options.body: Keep local login possible with a clear warning, accepting that users may still create wrong-host credentials that the gateway cannot use.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block auth login when node-host config points at a non-loopback gateway and instruct the user to run the command on the gateway host.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the recent maintainer draft repair and verification for this exact remote-node OAuth boundary.
